solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Making a comeback, arrival constrained by dumb mistake (7)

indicators.note: coming back means running the letters the other way
the arrival is held inside the word for dumb

blocks.note: dumb = unable to speak
arr. is the abbreviation printed on timetables for arrival

explanation.surface: A sports star's comeback is spoiled when a silly blunder holds up their return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dumb' is not about silence in the story but a source of letters, and 'Making a comeback' is the step applied last, after the arrival is tucked in.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratum is an error, especially one listed for correction in a printed book.

clue.text: State test incorporating two separate elements (7)

indicators.note: the test takes the elements into its body

blocks.note: an exam is a test
Cl (chlorine) and I (iodine), chemical symbols placed at two separate points

explanation.surface: A test paper on chemistry in which two distinct elements appear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Separate' is the key: the two elements do not go into the test side by side but at two different points, so the chlorine and iodine are split by a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to state something, typically loudly or suddenly.

clue.text: Cheerful alternative, but not very advanced (5)

indicators.note: the word loses the letters for very and advanced

blocks.note: a variant is an alternative version
V = very, A = advanced; both removed from the front

explanation.surface: Someone offers a more upbeat option that is only modestly forward-thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: RIANT is a rare literary word, borrowed from French, meaning smiling or cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Riant means laughing or cheerful, from the French rire, to laugh.

clue.text: Lie about second-class syllabus (5)

indicators.note: the lie goes around the letter

blocks.note: a tale is a lie, as in telling tales
B is second class, after A

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone is misrepresenting a course of study as second-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie' wants to be a verb; here it is the noun, a fib.
explanation.definitionFit: A table, as in a schedule or timetable of topics, can set out what a course covers.

clue.text: Prima ballerina’s distinction at an end according to gossip (7)

indicators.note: gossip is talk, so the word is heard rather than read

blocks.note: a mark of distinction
over = finished; spoken in a British accent it sounds like OVA

explanation.surface: Talk has it that a great dancer's celebrated career is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: Alicia Markova was a celebrated English prima ballerina. The sound match needs a non-rhotic accent, where the final R of OVER is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Alicia Markova was one of the great prima ballerinas of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Characteristic of one pair of diamonds held by one pair of spades (7)

indicators.note: the diamonds sit inside ONE

blocks.note: D = diamonds, twice
ONE taken as written, then S = spades twice; ONE holds the DD

explanation.surface: A card player describes a hand in which a pair of diamonds sits with a pair of spades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' appears twice with different jobs: the first belongs to the definition, since the number one is odd; the second is the literal word that holds DD.
explanation.definitionFit: One is an odd number, so oddness is one of its defining properties.

clue.text: Greasy member putting down one adult source of games? (7)

indicators.note: in a down entry, moving the I further down the word

blocks.note: OILY, with its I moved down past the member
an MP is a Member of Parliament
the I from OILY, put down below MP
A = adult, the film rating

explanation.surface: An oily limb that turns out to be where some games come from.
explanation.walkthrough: OILY plus MP gives OILYMP; the I is then dropped lower to give OLYMPI, and A finishes it. Olympia in Greece was the site of the ancient Olympic Games.
explanation.definitionFit: The Olympic Games take their name from Olympia, where they were held in ancient Greece.

clue.text: Extremely loud engine DAF redesigned (9)

indicators.note: the letters are rebuilt into a new arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: A lorry maker's reworked engine turns out to be ear-splitting.
explanation.walkthrough: DAF is a Dutch truck maker, which makes the surface about vehicles; the capitals are there to hide that the name is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Deafening describes a noise loud enough to make you temporarily deaf.

clue.text: Base, drunk Heather reveals secrets to a few (9)

blocks.note: e is the base of natural logarithms
a sot is a drunkard
Erica is the botanical name for heather

explanation.surface: A low, tipsy woman called Heather lets confidential things slip to a select group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like an anagram signal, but it is the noun SOT. Heather is capitalised to pass as a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoterica are items or knowledge meant for, or understood by, only a small inner circle.

clue.text: Bone needs hard lump shaved (7)

indicators.note: trimmed at both edges, losing its outer letters

blocks.note: stern = hard, severe
LUMP without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A bone with a hard lump on it needs smoothing down.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the outer letters are the ones thrown away, and the middle UM is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: sternum is the anatomist's name for the flat breastbone in the chest.

clue.text: Clubs promoted Chuck, maybe for something with saucy connotations? (9)

indicators.note: Chuck is one example of a Berry

blocks.note: C = clubs, the card suit
ran = promoted, as a campaign or a candidate
Chuck Berry, the rock and roll pioneer

explanation.surface: Nightclubs pushed a rock star's songs, perhaps for their suggestive lyrics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saucy' suggests innuendo, but cranberry sauce is the connection. 'Chuck' looks like a verb meaning throw; it is Chuck Berry.
explanation.definitionFit: Cranberry is best known as the sauce served with turkey, hence its saucy associations.

clue.text: Stay over when daughter’s ousted Victor (5)

indicators.note: the daughter has pushed out Victor and taken his place

blocks.note: above = over
D = daughter
V is Victor in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A father sleeps over at his daughter's house after she threw out a man named Victor.
explanation.walkthrough: D replaces the V in ABOVE. 'Stay' looks like a verb, but the answer is the noun: an abode is a stay, a place of residence.
explanation.definitionFit: An abode is a place where one stays or lives; the old sense of abide is to stay.

clue.text: Style shown by TV duo, the first having a change of heart when given Oscar (3,4)

indicators.note: the middle letter of the first name is swapped
something given is handed over and added, so the O is tacked on at the end

blocks.clueFragment: TV duo, the first having a change of heart
blocks.note: ANT of Ant and Dec, with its middle N changed to R
the second of Ant and Dec
O is Oscar in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A TV double act's taste in design, with one of them changing his mind after winning an Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a hugely popular British TV presenting pair. 'Change of heart' is the key: ANT's heart, N, becomes R.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the geometric look of 1920s and 1930s design is one named style among many.

clue.text: Fantastic entrée after a drop of Penderyn, twelve years old? (3-4)

indicators.note: wildly imagined, so the letters are rearranged
the rearranged word follows the P
just the first bit of the whisky

blocks.note: the first letter of Penderyn
ENTREE rearranged

explanation.surface: A superb starter served after a dram of whisky aged twelve years.
explanation.walkthrough: Penderyn is a Welsh whisky, and 'twelve years old' reads as a whisky's age statement. It is really a child just short of the teens.
explanation.definitionFit: At twelve a child is a pre-teen, just below thirteen; the question mark flags the whisky pun.

clue.text: Spanish woman embraces male compatriot in grass (9)

indicators.note: Maria holds Juan in her arms

blocks.note: a typical Spanish woman's name
a typical Spanish man's name

explanation.surface: A Spanish woman hugs a fellow Spaniard on a lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In grass' seems to set the scene on a lawn; grass is the slang definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang sense: the dried leafy drug has long gone by the street name grass.

clue.text: Ascent overwhelming American – that guy’s gonna cause trouble (5,4)

indicators.note: the ascent swallows the American

blocks.note: a rise is an ascent
A = American
HE'LL = he will, that guy is going to

explanation.surface: A climb swamping an American, and some bloke is about to kick up a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: The chatty 'that guy's gonna' is a spelled-out contraction: he will, HE'LL.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: kicking up a loud, riotous fuss is making trouble in its noisiest form.

clue.text: Recklessly went in front of Lincoln and Ford et al? (9)

definitions.text: Recklessly went in front of Lincoln and Ford et al?

blocks.note: the surface reading is a line-up of US presidents, Abraham Lincoln and Gerald Ford among them
the setter means the car makes Lincoln and Ford: stepping carelessly out in front of traffic

explanation.surface: Someone rashly stood before two American presidents and their colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln and Ford read as US presidents, but they are car makes. Stepping carelessly across a road in front of cars is jaywalking.
explanation.definitionFit: To jaywalk is to cross a road recklessly, ignoring the traffic and the crossings.

clue.text: Documents island dialect (5)

blocks.note: ID = identity documents
IOM = Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Someone records the local speech of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Documents' looks like a verb; it is the noun giving ID. The Isle of Man is a self-governing island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is the particular language or dialect of a people or place.

clue.text: Cleaner fastidiously scrubbing recycled tin (5)

indicators.note: rubbing out letters from the word
the letters of TIN turn up in another order

blocks.note: daintily = fussily, fastidiously
TIN rearranged, removed from DAINTILY

explanation.surface: A cleaner meticulously scouring a used can.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily is British slang for a cleaner who comes in each day. The letters removed are not in the order TIN, which is why 'recycled' is there.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a daily is a domestic cleaner who comes in by the day.

clue.text: Denies connection with police officers gobbling spread (7)

indicators.note: the officers eat up the spread

blocks.note: DIs = detective inspectors
seed is sown, spread over the field

explanation.surface: Suspects deny links to police officers who were greedily eating a buffet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' tempts as a meal to gobble; it is the past participle of sow.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown someone is to deny any connection with them.

clue.text: Send a message to us (9)

blocks.note: the verb for sending word down a wire in Morse, or signalling something in advance
the newspaper speaking of itself, as the paper this puzzle ran in

explanation.surface: A plain request to get in touch with the people writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Us' is the newspaper speaking: this puzzle appeared in the Daily Telegraph.
explanation.definitionFit: To telegraph is to send a message by telegram; the Telegraph is the paper printing the clue.

clue.text: Boring outside broadcast (7)

indicators.note: sown far and wide, so scattered

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.surface: A dull outside broadcast from a TV crew on location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside broadcast' is a fixed TV phrase, which hides that 'broadcast' is working on 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something that drags on so long it wears you out is dull.

clue.text: Circular feature of plant … (7)

blocks.note: the noun: a printed handout delivered to many homes
the botanist's word for each small leaf-like division of a compound leaf

explanation.surface: A curved part of a plant, the thought trailing on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circular' looks like an adjective; it is the noun, a printed handout. The dots link this clue with 20 down, whose answer is also a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaflet is a printed circular, and also one of the small divisions of a compound leaf.

clue.text: … one that’s straight up, though not large (7)

definitions.note: 'one' stands for a plant, carried over from 19 down

indicators.note: the word is taken without the L

blocks.note: 'straight up' is British slang for honestly
L = large, removed

explanation.surface: Continuing 19 down: an upright plant, though not a big one.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots make 'one' mean a plant from the previous clue. Honesty is a garden plant with flat, papery, coin-shaped seed pods.
explanation.definitionFit: Honesty (Lunaria) is a garden plant grown for its silvery disc-shaped seed pods.

clue.text: Tricky situation difficult when hotel’s sacked sommelier? (7)

indicators.note: the hotel letter is dismissed from the word

blocks.note: to be in a stew is to be in a fix
hard = difficult
H is Hotel in the NATO alphabet, removed from HARD

explanation.surface: An awkward moment at a hotel after the wine waiter is fired.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: a sommelier is a wine steward.
explanation.definitionFit: A sommelier is a wine steward, the restaurant staff member in charge of wine.

clue.text: Unknown detective plugs articles about lost people (7)

indicators.note: the unknown and the detective fill a gap between the articles

blocks.note: A and AN, both forms of the indefinite article, which open to take the plug
z is an unknown in algebra
tec is slang for detective

explanation.surface: An unidentified sleuth promotes stories about people who went missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plugs' reads as advertising; it means filling a hole. The Aztecs are a lost civilisation, overthrown by the Spanish in the 1520s.
explanation.definitionFit: Aztecan means relating to the Aztecs, a people whose empire vanished after the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: Covering combined forces that move round without resistance (5)

indicators.note: the resistance letter is left out

blocks.note: torque is a turning force
R is the symbol for electrical resistance, removed

explanation.surface: Allied troops on the move form a protective shield without meeting opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Combined forces' reads as a military alliance; in physics torque is the combined effect of forces causing rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: A toque is a small brimless hat, most familiar as a chef's tall white hat.

clue.text: Stopping for last game holds up church service? (5)

indicators.note: stopping a word at both ends cuts off its first and last letters
in a down entry, the game sits below and supports the church

blocks.note: CH = church
a last game is a FINAL; stopped at both ends it leaves INA

explanation.surface: Someone skipping the last round of play is keeping the congregation waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church service' reads as a single idea, but the service is a dinner service. The question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: China is porcelain tableware, and a set of it is a dinner or tea service.

clue.text: Republican blocks unconvincing cause (5)

indicators.note: the Republican sits in the middle, blocking the way

blocks.note: a weak argument is unconvincing
R = Republican

explanation.surface: A Republican politician obstructs a feeble campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cause' looks like a noun, a campaign; it is the verb, as in wreak havoc.
explanation.definitionFit: A collocation: this is the verb that goes with havoc or damage, meaning to inflict it.

clue.text: Censures half of rest after old boy left with nothing (9)

blocks.note: OB = old boy, a former pupil
L = left
O = zero, nothing
the first half of QUIESCENCE, rest

explanation.surface: Criticism for taking only half a break after a former pupil walked out empty-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of rest' needs the ten-letter word QUIESCENCE, not REST itself; its first five letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Obloquy is strong public censure or abuse; obloquies are instances of it.

clue.text: Slash hard bits from Unfinished Symphony (7)

indicators.note: just the first pieces of each word are taken

blocks.note: solid = hard
the first letters of Unfinished and Symphony

explanation.surface: Cut the difficult passages from Schubert's Unfinished Symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slash' reads as a command to cut; it is the name of the / symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A solidus is the oblique stroke /, also called a slash.

clue.text: Trim back, cutting your old treatment (7)

indicators.note: the letters run the other way
the reversed word cuts into the old possessive

blocks.note: thy = your, in old English
PARE (trim) reversed

explanation.surface: A barber's instruction to trim the back, then a remark on someone's old-fashioned beauty treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trim back' reads as a haircut instruction; 'back' is the reversal signal applied to PARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is treatment intended to heal or relieve a disorder.
